english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for making an uncertain conjecture or supposition.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for making a rough calculation or judgment.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for supposing something is true without proof.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for thinking or supposing that something is true.
This is the all-purpose everyday choice for inferring or guessing from incomplete evidence.
Use 估 as the all-purpose everyday way to say that you are guessing or putting forward an unproven idea.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for tentatively saying what you think is true.
Choose this when “suppose” means making an uncertain guess or assumption from incomplete information rather than simply saying what you think.
Use this for a tentative guess or supposition, rather than distrust or an accusation of guilt.
Use this when you are guessing or making an uncertain estimate.
